reasoning: Both attempts are correct and complete. Each raycasts every frame with the right exclusions, offsets along the normal, reuses PlacementRules, tears down fully, and has a typed class and an options table. B's failed 'disconnects' check isn't a real defect, because UnbindFromRenderStep stops the per-frame update just as fully. B adds a few extras: a guard against destroying twice, rejection reasons, and an inset to avoid z-fighting. But it breaks the project's conventions (Module table, const services, PascalCase method names), and its stand-in empty folder makes every spot look placeable until PlacedBlocks replicates. A is simpler, follows the conventions, and returns a clean Vector3? answer, so it's slightly more ready to merge.

criteria.note: `_Update` runs on RenderStepped. It raycasts from the mouse with the character and `_Part` excluded, snaps `result.Position + result.Normal * (BlockSize/2)`, unparents the part on a miss, styles it from `BlockTypes.Styles`, and lerps toward red when `PlacementRules.check` fails against PlacedBlocks.
`Destroy` disconnects `_RenderConnection` and destroys `_Part`. The class makes no other connections, so no frame update can run after teardown.
The `Fields` type with `typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, Module))` declares every field, all set in one literal in `new`. The part has CanCollide and CanQuery off and is also in the raycast filter.
`new(blockType: BlockType, options: Options?): GhostPreview` is typed, and `GetPlacement(): Vector3?` returns nil consistently whenever the spot isn't placeable.
An `Options` table carries `Transparency` and `RaycastDistance`, with defaults in the named constants `DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY` and `DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE`.
One class file, nothing out of scope, all tools pass, and it follows the repo conventions (a `Module` table and `const` services).

`_update` raycasts with the character and part filtered, steps half a block out along the normal before `snap`, hides the ghost on a miss with transparency 1, styles from BlockTypes, and tints with BLOCKED_COLOR when `check` fails.

`destroy` calls `UnbindFromRenderStep` with a unique bind name, destroys the part, and sets `_destroyed`, which `_update` checks. The failed 'disconnects' check only reflects that it uses BindToRenderStep instead of a connection.
`Fields` with `typeof(setmetatable(...))` declares every field, all set together in `new`. The part is non-colliding, has CanQuery off, and is filtered from the raycast.
`getPlacement(): (boolean, Vector3?, string?)` is a typed boolean plus optional position, with reason 'NoTarget' on a miss, and every method is typed.
An `Options` table carries `Transparency` and `MaxDistance`, with defaults in `DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY` and `DEFAULT_MAX_DISTANCE`.

Stays in scope and the tools pass, but it breaks repo conventions: the class table is named `GhostPreview` instead of `Module`, services use `local` instead of `const`, and method names are camelCase.

strengths: Clean, minimal design that does everything the task asks
Vector3? from GetPlacement is a simple, consistent answer for the controller
Rebuilds the raycast filter only when the character changes
weaknesses: Every spot shows as blocked until PlacedBlocks replicates (documented, but a little odd)
SetBlockType only shows on the next frame
Destroy has no explicit guard against being called twice, though calling it again is harmless

strengths: Destroy is idempotent behind a `_destroyed` guard
Updates right after the camera moves, so the ghost doesn't lag the view
Returns the rejection reason from check
Slight inset avoids z-fighting with neighboring blocks
weaknesses: Doesn't follow the project conventions (Module naming, const)
If PlacedBlocks hasn't replicated yet, the stand-in empty folder makes every spot look placeable
Builds a new filter table every frame
The hidden ghost stays parented in workspace
